RIVERA Member, Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP) Kabankalan Negros Occidental Dear SP Member Rivera: DILG Legal Opinion No. 5, S. 2014 10 FEB 2014 This refers to your IO December 2013 letter seeking this Department's opinion on whether the Commission on Audit's (COA) prescribed salary grade of a City Vice-Mayor (SG26/S1) prevails/supersedes Section 9 (a) of Republic Act No. 8297, otherwise known as the "Charter of the City of Kabankalan. " It is alleged in your letter that you were the Kabankalan City Vice Mayor from 01 July 1998 to 30 2007 and that from 01 July 1998 to 31 December 1999, you received an annual salary P243,348.00 corresponding to Salary Grade (SG) 28/SI. Allegedly, January 2000, the COA prescribed thé salary grade of the Vice Mayor as SCJ 26/S1 . 3=reafter, you received a compensation corresponding to SG 26/SI until the expiration ot your term on 30 June 2007. Hence, this request. Below are the following discussions that will help elucidate on the issue raised: Legal Bases of Local Elective Officials ' Compensation Republic No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" (hereinaftev "Code"), in relation to Republic Act No. 6758, otherwise known as the .!lld Position Classification Act of after, "RA 6758"), provides the compe 'en rate/salary grade of local elective officials based on the prescribed salary schey • Qs implemented by the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) pursuant to Administrative Order No. 42, s. 1993. The city vice-mayor's compensation is specifically governed by Section 456 (b) of the Code, vig.: "Section 456. No. 6758 and the implementing guidelines issued pursuant thereto. " (Underscoring ours)

The City Charter of Kab •alan Republic Act NO. 8297 (RA 8297), otherwise known as the "Charter of the City of Kabankalan, " converts the Municipality of Kabankalan into a component city of the -Province of Negros Occidental. Section 9 thereof prescribes the compensation rate of the city vice-mavor zs SG 28, viz.: be elected in the same manner as the city mayor and shall, at the time of his election, possess the same qualifications as the city mayor. He Shull hold office convensation corresponding to Salam/ Grade 'hoenft/-eigllt (28) as prescribed under Republic Act No. 6758, and the implementing guidelines issued pursuant thereto. xxx" (Underscoring ours) Section 456 of' the Code vis-å-vis Section 9 of 8297 It is a in statutory construction that "a general law and a special law on the same subject are in pari material and should, accordingly, be read together and harmonized, 9 possible, with a view to giving effect to both. " In Corona, et al. vs. Court of Appeals, et al. (G.R. No. 97356. 30 September 1992), the Supreme Court held that the assumption is that whenever the gislature enacts a law, it has in mind the previous statutes relating to the same subject matter, and in the absence of any express repeal or amendment, the new statute is deemed enacted in accordance with the legislative policy embodied in those prior statues. Moreover, in City of Naga, et al. vs. Agna, et al. (G.R. No. 36049. 31 May 1976), the Supreme COUrL held that in cases involving the harmonization of two or more laws relating to the same subject matter, the usual question is whether the later act has impliedly amended or repealed the earlier statute. A statute will not, however, be construed as prior act or acts on the same subject in the absence of words to that effect, unless law is evidently intended to supersede all prior acts on the matter and to compri .e itself the sole and complete system of legislation on the subject. Nonetheless, tikis also admits of the rule that if two or more laws on the same subject cannot possibly be reconciled or harmonized, one has to give way in favor of the other. In the case of two acts where one is a special law and the other general which, if standing -alone, would include that matter and thus conflict with the special act, the special must prevail since it evinces the legislative intent more clearly than that of a general statute.2 Notably, the Eide that the general law must yield to the special law in the specific and particular subject embraced in the latter, irrespective of the date of passage of the special law, is not absolute. One exception is that where the legislature clearly intended the later general to cover the whole subject and to repeal all prior laws inconsistent Statues are in N? •teria when they relate to the same person or thing, or have the same purpose or object, or cover the san.l specific or particular subject matter as held in City of-Naga vs. Agna (G.R. No. 36049, 31 May 1976) 2 Agpalo, Statutory Construction, 4111 Ed. (1998), p. 278

In such case, there is repeal of the special law.3 This exception obtains in the case of Section 456 (b) of the Code vis-å-vis 9 of RA 8297. Of particularly importance herein is Section 325 (b) of the Code, which includes as a general to the use of LGU funds, the proscription on conferring a higher salary rate than the maximum fixed for the position of an official or employee or other positions of equivalent rank, viz: "Section 325. General Limitations.- The use of the provincial, city, and nunicipal funds shall be subject to the following limitations: xxx (b) No o icial or ent 101 ee shall be entitled to a salar e higher than the maxilliJ!Y11 fixed for Ilis position or other positions of equivalent rank bu applica!Lie lacos or rules and regulations issued thereunder;" (Underscoring ours) This was amvt; fied in Administrative Order No. 42, s. 1993, entitled, Clarifying the Role of the Department of Budget and Management in the Compensation and Classification of Local Government Positions Under Republic Act No. 7160, which mandates the DBM, through its appropriate bureau, in the administration of the compensation and position classification systems in local government units. Clearly, the Code purposely intended for the uniformity of the salary grade of local elective and appointive officials/employee of equivalent rank as fixed by law or rules and regulations agued in relation thereto. In enacting RA 8297, it is assumed that the legislaiure did not intend to create an exception to Section 456 (b) of the Code as the -Code itself ch'arly and categorically provided a proscription in granting a salary rate higher than maximum fixed for the local elective and appointive official/employee's position or position of equivalent rank under Section 325') thereof. In view of the foregoing, the compensation rate/salary grade of a city vice-mayor of a component city is SG 26 as prescribed under the Code in relation to RA 6758. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly youxs, AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecret DI I-CEO USLG 201401.019 31bid., p.288
